newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds weaker in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds weaker in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed yield spreads remained mostly unchanged versus Treasuries despite a small drop in prices on Monday afternoon, traders said.
Market volume was thin as very few issues traded hands, they said.
"There's not too much going on really," said one trader at a large investment firm. "We traded off a little bit all day," he said.
The trader noted that 15-year mortgage paper looks attractive because of a 70- to 80-basis-point spread over comparable Treasuries coupled with dollar rolls trading below 5.0 percent.
"If you combine that total rate of return of the spread plus the roll, you are really looking at north of 100 basis points on 15-year paper, and we think that is pretty good," he said.
At 1545 EST/2045 GMT, mortgages were 1/32 to 4/32 lower across the board, while comparable Treasuries were down 2/32 to 3/32.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was 3/32 lower at 100-10/32, yielding 108 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were off 3/32 as well, at 100-04/32 and 100-08/32, respectively. The 10-year Treasury note was off 3/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
Traders said market activity will continue to be subdued as investors focus on Wednesday's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual testimony is scheduled to be heard by the Senate Banking Committee Wednesday and by the House on March 5.
